neighbours.label: A further conjunct opening after a completed 'X and Y' pair: ', and', ';' or ', as well as'
fire: The museum displays paintings and sculptures, as well as rare maps from Spain.
Our clinic treats asthma and allergies, as well as minor sports injuries.
She studied law and economics, and her sister became a doctor.
The report covers wages and prices; the appendix lists every source.
He repairs clocks and watches, and he teaches a class on Sundays.
The firm builds ships and cranes, as well as parts for trains.
Visitors praised the food and service; the rooms got lower marks.
Farmers here grow wheat and barley, and many also keep sheep.
quiet: The museum displays old paintings, as well as rare maps from Spain.
Our clinic treats severe asthma, as well as minor sports injuries.
She studied law in Madrid, and her sister became a doctor.
The report covers hourly wages; the appendix lists every source.
He repairs antique clocks, and he teaches a class on Sundays.
The firm builds large ships, as well as parts for trains.
Visitors praised the local food; the rooms got lower marks.
Farmers here grow winter wheat, and many also keep sheep.

notes: Probes: the same connective after a single noun read near zero, and after a pair 0.24-0.43. The + pole fires on ' and' extending a chain without a comma, which may be the other side of the distinction; not tested here.
